solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: One tendering rum as part of a recipe (10)

indicatorNotes.rum: rum means odd or strange, so the letters come out in a strange order

annotation.surface: Someone offering rum as one element of a cocktail recipe.
annotation.walkthrough: Rum sits in the surface as a drink you might put in a recipe; its crossword job is the adjective meaning odd.
annotation.definitionFit: A recipe lists the components of a dish, and each component is called an ingredient, as rum could be.

entries.clue: How do you rate Tibetan monk’s goodness? Capital! (9)

blocks.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
the question asks whether his goodness is bad

annotation.surface: Someone wondering how good a Tibetan monk is, then shouting that it is excellent.
annotation.walkthrough: Asking how you rate a monk's goodness is asking 'Is lama bad?', which run together spells the city. 'Capital!' looks like an exclamation of approval; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The exclamation is really the noun: Islamabad is the seat of government of Pakistan.

entries.clue: I’d gruel, bananas and bread somewhere once (7)

indicatorNotes.bananas: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: A menu of gruel, bananas and bread from some bygone place.
annotation.walkthrough: Bananas and bread look like more food in the list; bread is slang for money, and bananas is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: The guilder was the currency (bread, slang for money) of the Netherlands before the euro.

entries.clue: Tiny city in Northern Ireland one thus must enter (8)

indicatorNotes.must enter: enter places I and SO inside the city

blocks.note: Derry (Londonderry), a city in Northern Ireland

annotation.surface: A small Northern Irish city with an entry requirement.
annotation.walkthrough: Derry is the everyday name for Londonderry; 'tiny' as in a derisory offer, laughably small.
annotation.definitionFit: A derisory amount is so small as to be laughable.

entries.clue: Medical expert upset doctors in legion (15)

indicatorNotes.upset: upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A specialist annoyed at how many doctors there are.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes upset an emotion and doctors a profession, matching the definition, so the fodder hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: An endocrinologist is a doctor specialising in hormones and glands.

entries.clue: What’s proposed in London Washington’s declined to discuss (6)

blocks.note: in British usage, to table a motion is to put it forward
in American usage, to table a motion is to shelve it

annotation.surface: A British proposal that the Americans refuse to talk about.
annotation.walkthrough: The same verb means opposite things on either side of the Atlantic, and London and Washington signal which usage each half wants.
annotation.definitionFit: Tabled means put forward for discussion in Britain but postponed indefinitely in the US.

entries.clue: Land ultimately not high? Just the opposite (4)

annotation.definition: Land ultimately not high? Just the opposite

indicatorNotes.Just the opposite: the opposite order of what has been built, so it is turned around

annotation.surface: A remark that some ground isn't high after all, then a correction that it is.
annotation.walkthrough: Read straight, the clue describes the answer too: land that is just the opposite of not high, so high ground.
annotation.definitionFit: A wold is upland, a stretch of high open country as in the Cotswolds, the opposite of low ground.

entries.clue: Struggle with supporting public’s outlook on life (5-4)

indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down answer, a supporting piece sits underneath

blocks.note: the world = the public, as in 'the whole world knows'

annotation.surface: Wrestling with how the public sees life.
annotation.walkthrough: The possessive on public leans on the world meaning everyone; in a down clue, supporting puts the rest underneath.
annotation.definitionFit: The term translates the German Weltanschauung, a philosophy of life.

entries.clue: Scholarly poet and his familiar address? (7)

blocks.note: Ned is a familiar form of Edward

annotation.surface: A bookish poet and the nickname his friends used.
annotation.walkthrough: 'His' ties the address to the poet: Edward Lear's pet name is Ned. 'Address' is the way you address him, not where he lives.
annotation.definitionFit: Learned (two syllables) means scholarly, having much knowledge.

entries.clue: Having spare time, the French made certain to be down by noon (8)

indicatorNotes.to be down by: down by means short of, so N is taken away

blocks.note: n = noon; removed from INSURED leaving ISURED

annotation.surface: A French person with time off making sure to come downstairs by midday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Down by' reads as a deadline; here it means INSURED is short of its N.
annotation.definitionFit: Leisured means having ample free time.

entries.clue: Somewhere off the beaten track, unknown in part of Norfolk? (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the unknown goes in the Norfolk water

blocks.note: the Norfolk Broads are a network of rivers and lakes in eastern England; one is a broad
y = an unknown in algebra; goes inside BROAD

annotation.surface: A remote, undiscovered spot in the Norfolk countryside.
annotation.walkthrough: The Broads are the lakes and waterways of Norfolk, each one a broad; Y goes after its B.
annotation.definitionFit: A byroad is a minor road away from the main routes.

entries.clue: Style of cut — on the ears (4)

indicatorNotes.on the ears: as heard, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

annotation.surface: A haircut trimmed around the ears.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a hairstyle; 'cut' is really grass that has been mowed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in 'mode of dress', from the French word for fashion.

entries.clue: Getting on, becoming king? (10)

blocks.note: an heir follows the monarch on to the throne

annotation.surface: An ageing heir finally ascending the throne.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting on' suggests growing old, fitting a long-waiting heir; it means prospering.
annotation.definitionFit: Succeeding means both doing well and following someone into office.

entries.clue: Tit? Wit? Nit? (9)

annotation.walkthrough: Three rhyming insults look like a list of synonyms; only the last is the definition, and the first two build the answer. A nit is a fool in British slang.
annotation.definitionFit: A birdbrain is a silly, stupid person, just like a nit.

entries.clue: Drug like it is containing animal’s skin (9)

indicatorNotes.containing: IT IS holds the next piece inside
indicatorNotes.skin: the skin of a word is its outer letters

blocks.note: dig = like, as in 'I dig it'
outer letters of animal, placed inside IT IS

annotation.surface: A drug that is like one containing animal hide.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Like' is the slang verb, as in 'I dig that', not a comparison; 'skin' means just the outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The drug takes the foxglove's Latin name, the plant it is extracted from.

entries.clue: Men banned from Berkshire town coming to blows (5)

indicatorNotes.banned from: the men are kept out of the town, so removed

blocks.note: Windsor, the Berkshire town with the royal castle
OR = other ranks, i.e. soldiers who are not officers; removed

annotation.surface: Men barred from a Berkshire town end up fighting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coming to blows' reads as a brawl; 'blows' is the noun, strong gusts. Berkshire is a county west of London.
annotation.definitionFit: A blow is a strong wind, so blows are winds.
annotation.definitionNote: blows is used as a plural noun (gales), not the verb

entries.clue: How worms appear in some parts (9)

annotation.definition: How worms appear in some parts

blocks.note: the surface asks where or when worms turn up
read literally, the body itself is in several parts, ringed sections

annotation.surface: Where worms turn up in certain regions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In some parts' seems to mean in certain places; it describes a body divided into parts.
annotation.definitionFit: An earthworm's body is made of ring-like sections, and divided into sections is exactly what segmented means.

entries.clue: Restore wave energy replacing both uranium and third of coal (8)

indicatorNotes.replacing both: E takes the place of both of the named letters, so it goes in twice

blocks.note: U = uranium; the second U of UNDULATE goes
third letter of coal; replaced by E

annotation.surface: A plan to bring back wave power in place of nuclear and coal.
annotation.walkthrough: In UNDULATE, the second U and the A each become E. The surface is energy policy, which hides that uranium is just its symbol.
annotation.definitionFit: A computing term: to recover a file that was deleted.

entries.clue: Stoop arrangement overlooking heart of Louisiana (5)

indicatorNotes.overlooking: overlooking means ignoring, so the letter is left out

annotation.surface: Arranging a porch that looks out over the middle of Louisiana.
annotation.walkthrough: A stoop is a porch in American English, which suits Louisiana; here it is the verb meaning to lower oneself.
annotation.definitionFit: To deign is to stoop to do something beneath one's dignity.

entries.clue: Mostly put off about careless climbing in the heights (7)

indicatorNotes.Mostly: most of the word, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.about: the first piece goes around the second
indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down answer, climbing means read upwards

blocks.note: DETER = put off, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Being deterred by someone clumsy on a mountain climb.
annotation.walkthrough: DET(LAX)E is built first, then the whole thing is read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Exalted means raised to a high rank or position.
annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a phrase meaning placed high, standing for the adjective

entries.clue: Declining movement when on course (9)

blocks.note: a fall in prices or fortunes
on a golf course, the club's stroke down towards the ball

annotation.surface: A decline that happens while things are on track.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Movement' serves both halves; the course is a golf course.
annotation.definitionFit: A downswing is both a decline and the downward stroke in golf.

entries.clue: Broadcast lazy viewers greatly admire (7)

indicatorNotes.Broadcast: broadcast means sent out as sound

annotation.surface: Couch potatoes adoring what's on television.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is TV viewers; the viewers are literally eyes.
annotation.definitionFit: An idol is someone worshipped, so the verb means to hero-worship.

entries.clue: Know boy brought up in town (6)

indicatorNotes.brought up: in a down answer, brought up means turned to read upwards

blocks.note: ken = know, in Scots and old English

annotation.surface: Recognising a lad who was raised locally.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' reads as raised in the town; it turns LAD upwards. Kendal is a market town in Cumbria, known for mint cake.
annotation.definitionFit: Kendal is a town in the English Lake District.

entries.clue: Put up a fight about trapping old game no more (10)

indicatorNotes.trapping: to trap something is to catch and hold it, so RE holds O inside

annotation.surface: Someone who resisted being caught in an old game, and now won't play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put up a fight about' looks like one phrase, but the fight is complete before 'about' starts the next piece. 'No more' tells you the game is obsolete.
annotation.definitionFit: Battledore was an old game, a forerunner of badminton played with a bat and shuttlecock.

entries.clue: Head of English government ministry returned (4)

indicatorNotes.returned: returned means sent back, so the letters read in reverse

annotation.surface: The head of an English government department comes back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head of' looks like a first-letter instruction; Head alone is the definition, slang for the skull.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang for the skull, by its rounded shape.

entries.clue: Impassive stone idol is moving (6)

indicatorNotes.is moving: moving means the letters shift about

blocks.note: st = stone, the unit of weight

annotation.surface: An expressionless statue that nevertheless moves you.
annotation.walkthrough: Impassive stone suggests a statue, and moving an emotional effect; it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Stolid means calm and showing little emotion.

entries.clue: Impractical individual that is hosting 500 top celebrities (8)

indicatorNotes.hosting: a host has guests inside the home, so IE takes D in

blocks.note: D = 500 in Roman numerals; goes inside IE
the A-list, the most famous people

annotation.surface: A dreamer throwing a party for 500 star guests.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface throws a party; 'top celebrities' is the A-list, the most sought-after guests.
annotation.definitionFit: An idealist pursues ideals rather than practical aims.

entries.clue: Twenty-four hours of seaside sun (4)

indicatorNotes.of: the answer is made of letters from the phrase that follows

annotation.surface: A day of sunshine at the beach.
annotation.walkthrough: The ides is a single day in the Roman calendar, which is why twenty-four hours can define it.
annotation.definitionFit: The ides is one day: the 15th of March, May, July or October, the 13th of other months.

entries.clue: Altered the revised printed paper (10)

indicatorNotes.revised: revised means reworked, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An editor tweaking a revised printed document.
annotation.walkthrough: Altered looks like the anagram signal; it is fodder, and revised does that job.
annotation.definitionFit: Letterhead is paper printed with a name and address at the top.
